## Design

### 2026-10-07 – I installed all the apps needed to start making my Starbie project. I installed Kicad and got my project up. Now I started making the schematic. I have no idea what I was doing at first, but a little

**2h**

I installed all the apps needed to start making my Starbie project. I installed Kicad and got my project up. Now I started making the schematic. I have no idea what I was doing at first, but a little research helped me be able to navigate Kicad on MacOS. It turns out that Kicad on Mac was a lot more inconvenient as you can only access the foot print and symbol libraries using hot keys. I'm genuinely surprised that they didn't include the tabber on the tab like the Linux and Windows version.

### 2026-10-08 – Ok this took me a really long time, because I was a little sick, so I couldn't figure some easy things out. I was figuring where the heck you get these blue Xs from, then I realized pressing Q creates

**4h**

Ok this took me a really long time, because I was a little sick, so I couldn't figure some easy things out. I was figuring where the heck you get these blue Xs from, then I realized pressing Q creates them; big brainfart. Then I finished the schematic and I was really happy. However, I then started working on the PCB editor and I spent most of my time designing a board that would fit all the parts as well as giving those connector lines the best possible path. Oh yeah, don't forget to mention the BUTTONS. I'd say the figuring out the buttons was my greatest achievement yet at trouble-shooting. The Sw2 button was connecting correctly on the pcb editor, then I realized it was in form B not A, and I Was like BRO. so I changed it and it connects well now...
